subject: Order Form: proposed split pay-cycle and VAT responsibility (clarify)
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@harborai.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: finance@harborai.com
Date: Thu, 21 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify invoicing path & VAT on Order Form (Harbor AI)

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks for the draft order form. A few questions from our finance team so we can route PO and VAT correctly:

- We need to confirm whether invoices will be issued from Redwood US entity (Redwood, Inc.) or Redwood EU entity (Redwood EU Ltd). Harbor will prefer an EU-origin invoice for VAT purposes if possible.
- For the minimum commit: can you outline a phased invoice cadence? Our procurement prefers staged invoices aligned with capacity tranches (quarterly) rather than a single upfront invoice.
- Net terms: can we get net 45 rather than net 30?
- Any VAT reverse-charge applicability? We need the language to be explicit in the order form appendix so our VAT team can sign off.

Can you send a clean payment schedule we can circulate internally? Also flag any tax evidence we should prepare.

Best,
Marta Lopez
Finance Director, Harbor AI
Attachments: harbor-internal-vat-ask.pdf
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@harborai.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 21 Aug 2025 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify invoicing path & VAT on Order Form (Harbor AI)

Marta —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick answers and next steps below; I'll attach a proposed payment schedule for your review.

1) Invoice origin: we can issue from Redwood EU Ltd (our Luxembourg entity) — we'll reflect this as the default invoice payee in the order form. If Harbor still needs Redwood, Inc. invoices for accounting reasons, we can add an invoice recipient field per invoice (see option B in the attached).

2) Minimum commit phasing: attached is a two-option schedule: (A) Quarterly tranche invoices tied to minimum commit milestones; (B) Monthly tranche with a deposit + monthly true-up. Option A aligns with your ask.

3) Net terms: we can support net 45 for EU customers pending quick credit check (internal approval). I'm marking this as a conditional exception and will escalate to finance.

4) VAT reverse-charge: from our initial read, reverse-charge may apply depending on Harbor's VAT registration and the service classification. We will add a short VAT appendix that: (a) declares Redwood EU as invoice issuer, (b) includes a checkbox to apply reverse-charge if Harbor provides VAT reg. No tax opinion included — Harbor should confirm with local counsel.

Attachments: proposed_payment_schedule_v1.xlsx

Next steps: Ben will attach the MSA redline with the invoice-recipient clause and I will loop in accounting for the net-45 exception. If these options look good I can produce an updated order form (clean + redline) for signature.

Cheers,
Kimberly Park
Director, Contracts & Pricing
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@harborai.com>, finance@harborai.com
Date: Thu, 21 Aug 2025 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify invoicing path & VAT on Order Form (Harbor AI)

Kim / Marta —

Quick add from pricing/ops:
- Recommend Option A (quarterly tranche invoices) but with an initial 10% deposit invoice at contract effective date to cover provisioning. That reduces billing churn and matches capacity allocation.
- On net terms: we'll tentatively accept net 45 for the EU entity if Harbor provides credit references. I'll include a short clause in MSA redline that ties net-term exceptions to a credit approval sub-process.
- Tax evidence: Harbour's VAT cert + company registration (EU VAT ID) and a billing contact for reverse-charge. If Harbor prefers Redwood US invoices, VAT implications differ — we'll note both flows in the appendix.

Attaching redline: MSA_redline_KP_BC_20250821.docx (MSA section 2.4 invoice recipient + section 7 tax).

Ben
Sr. Commercial Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
Attachments: MSA_redline_KP_BC_20250821.docx

Subject: Re: Clarify invoicing path & VAT on Order Form (Harbor AI)

Thanks Kim/Ben — a few clarifying points from Harbor finance after reading the proposed schedule and redline:

- The EU entity invoice option is preferred. Harbor can provide VAT registration (EU VAT ID) and will confirm reverse-charge eligibility.
- The 10% deposit is acceptable. Can you itemize how deposit will be applied against the first tranche in the schedule? We need a line item on the invoice to show deposit credit.
- Net 45: Harbor needs written confirmation that credit checks are limited to standard trade references (no bureau pull). If acceptable, we'll proceed.
- Invoice recipient: Harbor will request invoices be addressed to Harbor AI Ltd (Ireland) and sent to ap-invoices@harborai.com. Please confirm email routing and whether a PDF invoice + machine-readable XML can be supported for our ERP.

Appreciate the speed on this. If you can update the order form appendix to include: invoice recipient field, deposit application line, and a VAT checkbox, we can move to approvals on our side.

Regards,
Harbor Finance (on behalf of Marta Lopez)
Attachments: harbor-vat-registration-sample.pdf
